issue: h₂éryomes 'we plough': root is *h₂erh₃- (Lat. arō, Gk. aróō); present should be *h₂érh₃yomes (the lexicon's h₂éryeti drops the h₃).

Notation only: unaccented tom and wewked, final -d in wewked, a-vowel h₁yáǵ-. This is a Lühr/Byrd-type reconstruction and is grammatical (accusative of the addressee with a verb of speaking, as in Byrd), but it does not match the corpus's accented notation.

Notation mixed within one sentence: h₁ékʷoybʰyos (with kʷ and the Indo-Iranian dat. pl. -bʰyos) next to h₁éḱwoms; agʰnutor has no laryngeal or accent (*h₂gʰnutór); wewked unaccented. Older scholarly (Schleicher-fable) notation, not the corpus's.
bʰréh₂tr̥s is gen./abl. sg.; 'said to the brother' needs dat. bʰréh₂trey. The speech tag 'said the brother' is also dropped.
bʰindth₂é is the 2sg middle past ('you split'); 'it split' needs 3sg bʰindtó (or aorist bʰidtó).

sréwmn̥h₂ pléh₁t 'the streams filled' uses the transitive root aorist ('fill X', Ved. aprāt). Intransitive 'became full' would be middle or the -dʰe- stem pléh₁dʰet, which the corpus itself uses in b86d64c4.
Hrugʰéys is gen./abl. sg. but is used as the subject of h₁syéh₁t; needs nom. Hrugʰís. Also wékʷos moy = 'my word', but the English has 'our word' (needs nos).
dh₃té is the 2pl imperative, addressed to a single god; needs 2sg dh₃dʰí (or duh₃dʰí).
yémHos (2x, nom. sg.) has root accent; the lexicon and Ved. yamá- have *yemHós, and the corpus elsewhere has yemHóh₁. One-twin suitor episode is otherwise fine.

dm̥h₂tóm is a root-aorist 2du (='you tamed' / 'tame!'), but the English has present 'you who tame' (present stem would be dm̥néh₂-); h₂éǵetes/duktés use 2du -tes, which is the 3du ending (handbook 2du *-th₁es); déh₃torh₁ for the dual is better *déh₃toreh₁ (Ved. dātārā).
súHnu voc.: Ved. sūno, Lith. sūnaũ, OCS synu point to a full-grade-suffix *suHnéw/-ów; a bare-stem vocative is the Greek-type minority view.

Laryngeal-less, augmented Lehmann–Zgusta notation (owis, aǵrom, ebʰuget for *h₂ówis, *h₂éǵrom); masc. ptcp. ḱeḱluwōs with owis, which is feminine in this lexicon (fem. would be *ḱeḱluwusih₂). Clashes with the corpus's notation.
h₁ń̥gʷni voc.: the Vedic vocative of this very word is ágne, which points to *h₁n̥gʷney (i-stem voc. *-ey); a bare-stem -i is the Greek type.
h₁stā́m is 3du imperfect, but the subject gʷówes is plural; needs 3pl h₁sént.

stunédtu is a 3sg imperative, but h₂ékʷeh₂es is an animate (feminine) nom. pl., so the neuter-plural rule does not apply; needs 3pl stundéntu. Lesser points: déh₂n̥wi is an odd locative of an u-stem (*déh₂new(i)); h₁yód for 'if' is acceptable on the model of Ved. yád.

h₂wérst 'rains' is a past/injunctive form, while every other verb in the gnomic hymn is present (present stem *h₂wérseti). Active pékʷonti is 'they cook' (transitive), but the English 'the apples ripen' needs an intransitive middle (cf. Ved. pácyate).
ǵʰémi 'on Earth' drops the initial dʰ; the locative is *dʰǵʰém(i) (Ved. kṣámi, Hitt. taknī). The simplified form is a Latin/Balto-Slavic development (humī).
